title: Priority-aware KV eviction tuning to restore TTFT across mixed short/long sessions
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Summary: Multiple customers (hosted + Dedicated tenants + one Private deployment) reported sudden first-token latency regressions for short, interactive sessions after last week's kernel migration. Symptoms: elevated TTFT (first-byte) for short exchanges (~1-6 tokens) while long context/long-running sessions unchanged. Impacted models: rw-7b-v0.9 quant and openlm-13b-8bit variants under multiplexing. We observed median TTFT increase from ~80ms to ~170ms and P95 from ~420ms to ~1.1s for short sessions on affected workers. Root cause hypothesis: the new eviction heuristic in kv-cache favored LRU time-of-use only, which causes policy inversion under mixed workloads — long, heavy requests pin large KV shards and evict many small short-session entries. These short sessions then must re-prefetch KV on each request causing repeated cold-starts and higher per-request kernel overhead. Proposed fix: implement a priority-aware eviction bias that factors session priority and per-session token rate into eviction score (score = alpha * last_access + beta * size + gamma * session_priority). Also add a short-session prewarm bucket and a soft-reservation mechanism for small KV entries (<= 64KB) to avoid thrashing. Technical plan: 1) Add priority field to session metadata in router (keep default priority=1, customer-assigned priority for enterprise tenants). 2) Modify kv-eviction comparator in runtime to include session_priority and recent token-rate decayed counter. 3) Implement a small prewarm pool per-worker (configurable, default 8MB) for rapid short-session reuse. 4) Add a circuit-breaker to disable prewarm if overall memory pressure > 85% to avoid OOMs. Rollout: 1) Unit tests + integration tests (kv correctness, eviction invariants). 2) Staging canary on 10 workers in eu-west with mix of synthetic short/long workload. 3) Canary metrics to watch: TTFT P50/P95 for sessions < 6 tokens, tokens/sec, re-prefetch rate, overall worker memory. 4) Gradual 5/25/100 worker ramp with automatic rollback on >10% TTFT regression against baseline or memory pressure alerts. Customer communications: draft sent to affected customers (AcmeMaps, SecureChat Inc, EnterpriseBank) with explanation and ETA for fix. Monitoring/alerts: add dedicated dashboard and alert for short-session re-prefetch spike, new metric kv.prewarm_usage, and stickiness rate. Long-term follow-ups: evaluate combining with kernel prefetch hints and incorporate model-size-aware eviction weights. This ticket covers implementation + canary; follow-up epic will address enterprise policy UI and telemetry aggregation.
